protocolBuilder.arrayField.addRowTitle.description: Title of the dialog a researcher fills in to add a row to a list, where the list has offered no title of its own. itemLabel is the list’s own noun for one of its rows, already in the reader’s language.

protocolBuilder.arrayField.addSubmit.description: Button that commits the dialog a researcher has filled in for a NEW row of a list. The same dialog says Save when it is editing a row that already exists.

protocolBuilder.arrayField.editRow.description: Accessible name of the button that opens one row of a list in its editing dialog. itemLabel is the list’s own noun for one of its rows, already in the reader’s language.

protocolBuilder.arrayField.emptyState.defaultMessage: No items have been created yet.
protocolBuilder.arrayField.emptyState.description: Shown in place of the rows when a list has none, and the list’s caller has offered no wording of its own.

protocolBuilder.arrayField.itemNoun.description: Generic noun for one row of an editable list in a stage editor, used where the list has no more specific word for its rows. Interpolated mid-sentence into things said ABOUT a row ("Remove this item?", "This item was not saved."), so it is lower case and singular.

protocolBuilder.arrayField.listDisabledR.defaultMessage: This list is not accepting changes at the moment, so this {itemLabel} was not saved. Copy anything you want to keep, then try again once the list can be edited.
protocolBuilder.arrayField.listDisabledR.description: Shown above the fields of a row editor when the list itself has stopped accepting changes — because something else on the stage that it depends on is no longer chosen — so the row could not be saved. itemLabel is the list’s own noun for one of its rows: "prompt", "option", "item".

protocolBuilder.arrayField.readOnlyRefus.defaultMessage: This stage is read-only, so this {itemLabel} was not saved. Take over editing and try again.
protocolBuilder.arrayField.readOnlyRefus.description: Shown to a researcher whose edit to one row of a list was refused because they no longer hold the right to edit the stage (one step of an interview). itemLabel is the list’s own noun for one of its rows, already in the reader’s language. Taking over editing is an action offered elsewhere in the host application.

protocolBuilder.arrayField.removalUnavai.defaultMessage: This list stopped accepting changes while you were confirming, so this {itemLabel} was not removed. Remove it again once the list can be edited.
protocolBuilder.arrayField.removalUnavai.description: Shown inside a removal confirmation when the list stopped accepting changes while the researcher was reading it, so nothing was deleted. itemLabel is the list’s own noun for one of its rows, already in the reader’s language.

protocolBuilder.arrayField.removeRow.description: Action that deletes one row of a list — the accessible name of the button on the row, and the confirm button of the confirmation it raises. itemLabel is the list’s own noun for one of its rows, already in the reader’s language.

protocolBuilder.arrayField.removeRowDesc.defaultMessage: This {itemLabel} will be removed from the list.
protocolBuilder.arrayField.removeRowDesc.description: Body of the confirmation raised when a researcher deletes one row of a list. itemLabel is the list’s own noun for one of its rows, already in the reader’s language.

protocolBuilder.arrayField.removeRowTitl.description: Title of the confirmation raised when a researcher deletes one row of a list. itemLabel is the list’s own noun for one of its rows, already in the reader’s language.

protocolBuilder.arrayField.reorderRow.description: Accessible name of the handle that drags one row of a list into a different position. itemLabel is the list’s own noun for one of its rows, already in the reader’s language; position is the row’s own place in the list, counting from one; count is how many rows the list holds.

protocolBuilder.arrayField.rowEditorFail.defaultMessage: This editor could not be shown, so there is nothing to fill in here. Close it and try again. If it keeps happening, the problem is in this interface’s editor rather than in your protocol.
protocolBuilder.arrayField.rowEditorFail.description: Shown in place of the fields of a row-editing dialog when the interface’s own editor code threw while rendering. Says the fault is in the software rather than in anything the researcher wrote, so they do not go looking for a mistake in their protocol.

protocolBuilder.arrayField.rowRemovedRef.defaultMessage: This {itemLabel} was removed while your changes were being saved, so there is nothing left to save them to. Copy anything you want to keep, then cancel and add a new {itemLabel}.
protocolBuilder.arrayField.rowRemovedRef.description: Shown to a researcher whose edit to one row of a list was saved after that row had already been deleted. itemLabel is the list’s own noun for one of its rows — "prompt", "option", "item" — already in the reader’s language.

protocolBuilder.arrayField.rowReplacedRe.defaultMessage: This {itemLabel} was replaced while you were confirming, so nothing was removed. Check the list and remove it again if you still want to.
protocolBuilder.arrayField.rowReplacedRe.description: Shown inside a removal confirmation when the row it was opened on has been replaced by a different one while the researcher was reading it, so nothing was deleted. itemLabel is the list’s own noun for one of its rows — "prompt", "option", "item" — already in the reader’s language.

protocolBuilder.arrayField.rowUnresolved.defaultMessage: This list changed while you were editing, so this {itemLabel} could not be matched to a row in it and nothing was saved. Copy anything you want to keep, then check the list and make the change again.
protocolBuilder.arrayField.rowUnresolved.description: Shown to a researcher whose edit could not be matched to any one row of the list, because the list moved while they were editing. itemLabel is the list’s own noun for one of its rows, already in the reader’s language.

protocolBuilder.arrayField.saveRefused.defaultMessage: This {itemLabel} could not be saved. Check your changes and try again.
protocolBuilder.arrayField.saveRefused.description: Shown above the fields of a row editor when saving was refused for a reason that gave no explanation of its own. The last resort. itemLabel is the list’s own noun for one of its rows.

protocolBuilder.assignAttributes.addButt.description: Visible text and accessible name of the button that adds another row to the list of attributes a prompt stamps onto every node it creates. Named in full rather than “Add new”, because a prompt editor mounts several lists side by side and a researcher navigating by buttons reads only these words.

protocolBuilder.assignAttributes.boolean.description: The other of the two values a prompt can stamp onto every node it creates, for an attribute that records a yes/no answer.
One of the two values a prompt can stamp onto every node it creates, for an attribute that records a yes/no answer. A prompt is the question a participant reads.

protocolBuilder.assignAttributes.deleteR.description: Accessible name of the button that removes one row from the list of attributes a prompt stamps onto the nodes it creates. It removes the row, not the attribute from the codebook.

protocolBuilder.assignAttributes.emptySt.description: Shown in place of the list while a prompt stamps nothing onto the nodes it creates. Not a problem to fix: assigning nothing is the ordinary case.

protocolBuilder.assignAttributes.listClo.defaultMessage: “{variableName}” was created, but this list stopped accepting changes while it was being created, so nothing has been assigned to it. Select “{variableName}” in the row you want it in once the list can be edited.
protocolBuilder.assignAttributes.listClo.description: Body of that notice, for when the list stopped accepting changes while the attribute was being created. variableName is the attribute name the researcher typed and is not translated.

protocolBuilder.assignAttributes.rowGone.defaultMessage: “{variableName}” was created, but the row it was created from is no longer in this list, so nothing has been assigned to it. Select “{variableName}” in the row you want it in.
protocolBuilder.assignAttributes.rowGone.description: Body of that notice, for when the row the researcher started from has left the list altogether. variableName is the attribute name they typed and is not translated.

protocolBuilder.assignAttributes.rowRepl.defaultMessage: The row you created “{variableName}” from was replaced while it was being created, so nothing has been assigned to it. Select “{variableName}” in the row you want it in.
protocolBuilder.assignAttributes.rowRepl.description: Body of that notice, for when the row the researcher started from has been replaced by a different one. variableName is the attribute name they typed and is not translated.

protocolBuilder.assignAttributes.unassig.description: Title of the notice shown when a codebook attribute the researcher created from a row was created successfully but could not be put into that row. variableName is the name they typed and is not translated.

protocolBuilder.assignAttributes.valueHi.defaultMessage: Every node created on this prompt is given this value.
protocolBuilder.assignAttributes.valueHi.description: Hint under the value control, saying what stamping means: a node is a member of the interview network, and a prompt is the question a participant reads.

protocolBuilder.assignAttributes.valueLa.description: Label of the control that chooses which value this row stamps onto every node the prompt creates.

protocolBuilder.assignAttributes.variabl.description: Label of the control that picks (or adds) the codebook attribute this row stamps onto every node the prompt creates.

protocolBuilder.attributeCodebookControl.defaultMessage: An attribute participants choose an answer from needs at least two values, so it is created together with them.
protocolBuilder.attributeCodebookControl.description: Shown above the buttons when the researcher is inventing an attribute whose answers come from a list, explaining why they are sent to the codebook editor rather than being asked for a name here.

protocolBuilder.attributeCodebookControl.defaultMessage: Create this attribute and its values
protocolBuilder.attributeCodebookControl.description: Button that opens the codebook editor for inventing an attribute whose answers are chosen from a list, together with that list. Also the title of the dialog it opens. An attribute is one thing an interview records about a network member.
The same button for a yes/no attribute, whose two stored values are fixed and whose WORDS are what a researcher writes — so this says labels rather than values. Also the title of the dialog it opens.
The same button for an attribute whose answer is not chosen from a list — a date between two bounds, a position on a scale. Also the title of the dialog it opens.
Button that opens the codebook editor for the rules a participant’s answer has to satisfy. Also the title of the dialog it opens.
Button that opens the codebook editor for the list of answers a participant chooses between. Also the title of the dialog it opens.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.affirmativ.defaultMessage: Choose the type of connection an affirmative answer creates.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.affirmativ.description: Refusal shown when a researcher saves a census prompt without saying what a yes from the participant records.
Heading of the group that says what a yes from the participant records between the people the prompt asked about.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.attributeC.description: Button that opens the codebook editor for inventing an attribute this prompt can write to. Also the title of the dialog it opens.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.attributeE.description: Button that opens the codebook editor for the list of answers the picked attribute offers, which are the bins or the points of the scale this prompt is answered on. Also the title of the dialog it opens.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.attributeL.description: Label of the control that picks which codebook attribute one prompt writes its answer to. An attribute is one thing an interview records about a network member.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.binAttribu.defaultMessage: Choose the attribute whose values become the bins.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.binAttribu.description: Refusal shown when a researcher saves a bin prompt without saying which attribute it sorts people by. A bin is one answer the participant drags a network member into.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.binDescrip.defaultMessage: Write the questions this stage asks about each person, and drag them into the order the participant answers them.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.binDescrip.description: Description of the prompts section in a stage where the participant answers each question about one network member at a time by dragging them into a bin. A stage is one step of an interview; a prompt is one question the participant is asked.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.binLimitTi.defaultMessage: More bins than fit on one screen
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.binLimitTi.description: Heading of the warning shown when the attribute a bin prompt uses offers more values than the interview screen can draw as bins.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.binOrderAd.defaultMessage: Add a rule for the order within a bin
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.binOrderAd.description: Button that appends one sort rule to the list ordering the people already dragged into a bin.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.binOrderDe.defaultMessage: Choose the order people already sorted into a bin are listed in.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.binOrderDe.description: Description of the group holding the rules that order the people already dragged into a bin.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.binOrderEm.defaultMessage: No rules yet, so people are listed in the order they were dropped in.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.binOrderEm.description: Shown in place of the sort rules ordering the people already dragged into a bin, when the researcher has written none.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.binOrderLa.defaultMessage: Rules for the order within a bin
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.binOrderLa.description: Label of the list of sort rules that order the people already dragged into a bin.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.binOrderTi.description: Heading of the optional group holding the rules that order the people already dragged into a bin.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.bucketOrde.defaultMessage: Add a rule for the order people are handed over in
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.bucketOrde.description: Button that appends one sort rule to the list ordering the people a bin stage has not been asked about yet.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.bucketOrde.defaultMessage: Choose the order the people still to be sorted are offered in.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.bucketOrde.description: Description of the group holding the rules that order the people a bin stage has not been asked about yet.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.bucketOrde.defaultMessage: No rules yet, so people are handed over in the order they were added.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.bucketOrde.description: Shown in place of the sort rules ordering the people a bin stage has not been asked about yet, when the researcher has written none.
Label of the list of sort rules that order the people a bin stage has not been asked about yet.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.bucketOrde.defaultMessage: Order people are handed to the participant in
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.bucketOrde.description: Heading of the optional group holding the rules that order the people a bin stage has not been asked about yet.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.defaultMessage: Choose the attribute whose values the participant sorts people into.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.description: Description of the group that picks the attribute whose values are the bins the participant drags people into. An attribute is one thing an interview records about a network member.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.defaultMessage: This type has no categorical attributes yet. Create one to say what the bins are.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.description: Shown in place of the attribute picker’s options when the node type this stage collects has no attribute whose answers come from a named list.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.defaultMessage: Each of this attribute's values becomes a bin, and dropping someone into a bin records that value for them.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.description: Guidance under the attribute picker in a Categorical Bin prompt, saying what happens to the attribute’s values in the interview.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.defaultMessage: The bins
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.description: Heading of the group that picks the attribute whose values are the bins the participant drags people into.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.defaultMessage: The participant sorts everyone into bins for one question at a time, in this order.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.description: Guidance under the list of prompts in a Categorical Bin stage, where a bin is one named answer the participant drags a network member into, and the bins have no order among them.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.defaultMessage: The participant drags each person into one of the bins below, so write a question the bins are the answers to — “what kind of contact do you have with this person?” rather than a yes or no question.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.description: Guidance shown above the box where a researcher writes a Categorical Bin prompt, saying what the participant does with it. The quoted sentence is an example of a question whose answers are the bins.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.defaultMessage: This interface is designed for up to eight bins, including a follow-up bin. Beyond that the bins become hard to read and hard to drop into, which costs data quality. Consider grouping the values and asking for the detail in a later question.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.description: Body of the warning shown when a Categorical Bin prompt would draw more bins than its interview screen is designed for. The follow-up bin is the extra one this prompt can add for answers none of the attribute’s values cover.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.defaultMessage: Create a new text attribute
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.description: Button that opens the codebook editor for inventing the text attribute the follow-up bin stores its answers in. Also the title of the dialog it opens.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.defaultMessage: This type has no text attributes yet. Create one to store what the participant types.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.description: Shown in place of the follow-up bin’s attribute options when the node type this stage collects has no attribute the participant can type into.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.defaultMessage: The participant types their own answer, so this is a text attribute.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.description: Guidance under the control that picks which attribute holds what the participant types into the follow-up bin, saying why only text attributes are offered.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.defaultMessage: Attribute the answer is stored in
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.description: Label of the control that picks which attribute holds what the participant types into the follow-up bin.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.defaultMessage: Choose the attribute this bin's answers are stored in.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.description: Refusal shown when a researcher switches the follow-up bin on and saves the prompt without saying where its answers are stored.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.defaultMessage: Set rules for what the participant types
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.description: Button that opens the codebook editor for the rules the participant’s typed answer has to satisfy. Also the title of the dialog it opens.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.defaultMessage: Shown on the bin itself, so it has to read as somewhere to put a person the other bins do not fit.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.description: Guidance under the box a researcher writes the follow-up bin’s own name into.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.defaultMessage: Bin label
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.description: Label of the box a researcher writes the follow-up bin’s own name into — the words drawn on that bin in the interview.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.defaultMessage: Other
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.description: Example name in the empty box where a researcher names the follow-up bin.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.defaultMessage: Name the bin the participant drops everyone else into.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.description: Refusal shown when a researcher switches the follow-up bin on and saves the prompt without naming it.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.defaultMessage: Add a bin for people none of the values above describe, and ask the participant what to record instead.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.description: Description of the optional group that adds one more bin for people none of the attribute’s values describe.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.defaultMessage: Asked as soon as someone is dropped into this bin.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.description: Guidance under the box a researcher writes the follow-up bin’s own question into, saying when the participant reads it.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.defaultMessage: Follow-up question
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.description: Label of the box a researcher writes the question asked as soon as the participant uses the follow-up bin.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.defaultMessage: What type of contact do you have with this person?
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.description: Example question in the empty box where a researcher writes the follow-up bin’s own question.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.defaultMessage: Write the question this bin asks.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.description: Refusal shown when a researcher switches the follow-up bin on and saves the prompt without writing the question it asks.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.defaultMessage: A bin for anything else
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.description: Heading of the optional group that adds one more bin for people none of the attribute’s values describe.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.defaultMessage: What type of contact do you have most with this person?
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.categorica.description: Example question in the empty box where a researcher writes a Categorical Bin prompt.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.dyadCensus.defaultMessage: Choose the kind of connection an affirmative answer records between the pair.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.dyadCensus.description: Description of the group that says what a yes from the participant records between the two people a Dyad Census prompt asked about.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.dyadCensus.defaultMessage: A connection of this type is created between the two people whenever the participant answers yes.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.dyadCensus.description: Guidance under the control that picks what a yes from the participant records between the two people a Dyad Census prompt asked about.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.dyadCensus.defaultMessage: The participant sees two people side by side and answers yes or no, so write the question about the pair in front of them — “these two people” rather than a name — and phrase it so that yes and no are both sensible answers.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.dyadCensus.description: Guidance shown above the box where a researcher writes a Dyad Census prompt, saying what the participant is looking at while they answer it. The quoted phrase is an example of how to refer to the pair.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.dyadCensus.defaultMessage: Do these two people know each other?
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.dyadCensus.description: Example question in the empty box where a researcher writes a Dyad Census prompt.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.edgeCreate.defaultMessage: Create a connection type and use it for this prompt
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.edgeCreate.description: Description at the top of the dialog for inventing a kind of connection, saying that the prompt will point at it once it exists.
Button that opens the codebook editor for inventing a kind of connection this prompt can record. Also the title of the dialog it opens.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.edgeLabel.description: Label of the control that picks which kind of connection between two people this prompt records. A connection is what the protocol schema calls an edge; the researcher never sees that word.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.oneToManyA.defaultMessage: Add a rule for the order people are asked about
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.oneToManyA.description: Button that appends one sort rule to the list ordering the people the participant is asked about.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.oneToManyA.defaultMessage: Choose the order the participant is asked about each person in.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.oneToManyA.description: Description of the group holding the rules that order the people the participant is asked about, one at a time.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.oneToManyA.defaultMessage: No rules yet, so people are asked about in the order they were added.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.oneToManyA.description: Shown in place of the sort rules ordering the people the participant is asked about, when the researcher has written none.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.oneToManyA.defaultMessage: Rules for the order people are asked about
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.oneToManyA.description: Label of the list of sort rules that order the people the participant is asked about, one at a time.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.oneToManyA.defaultMessage: Order of the people asked about
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.oneToManyA.description: Heading of the optional group holding the rules that order the people the participant is asked about, one at a time.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.oneToManyC.defaultMessage: Add a rule for the order people are shown in
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.oneToManyC.description: Button that appends one sort rule to the list ordering the people the participant picks from.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.oneToManyC.defaultMessage: Choose the order the people the participant selects from are shown in.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.oneToManyC.description: Description of the group holding the rules that order the people the participant picks from for whoever they were asked about.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.oneToManyC.defaultMessage: No rules yet, so people are shown in the order they were added.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.oneToManyC.description: Shown in place of the sort rules ordering the people the participant picks from, when the researcher has written none.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.oneToManyC.defaultMessage: Rules for the order people are shown in
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.oneToManyC.description: Label of the list of sort rules that order the people the participant picks from.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.oneToManyC.defaultMessage: Order of the people to choose from
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.oneToManyC.description: Heading of the optional group holding the rules that order the people the participant picks from for whoever they were asked about.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.oneToManyD.defaultMessage: Write the questions this stage asks about one person and the group around them, and drag them into the order the participant answers them.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.oneToManyD.description: Description of the prompts section in a stage that shows the participant one network member alongside all the others and asks which of the others the question applies to. A stage is one step of an interview; a prompt is one question the participant is asked.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.oneToManyE.defaultMessage: Choose the kind of connection an affirmative answer records between the two people.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.oneToManyE.description: Description of the group that says what selecting someone records between them and the person the prompt asked about.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.oneToManyE.defaultMessage: A connection of this type is created from the person being asked about to everyone the participant selects.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.oneToManyE.description: Guidance under the control that picks what selecting someone records between them and the person the prompt asked about.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.oneToManyF.defaultMessage: The participant is shown one person at a time and chooses who among the others the question applies to.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.oneToManyF.description: Guidance under the list of prompts in a One-to-Many Dyad Census stage, where the participant selects any number of the remaining network members for the person in front of them.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.oneToManyG.defaultMessage: The participant sees one person alongside everyone else and selects whoever the question applies to, so write it as a question about that one person and the group — “which of these people does this person know?” rather than a question about a single pair.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.oneToManyG.description: Guidance shown above the box where a researcher writes a One-to-Many Dyad Census prompt, saying what the participant is looking at while they answer it. The quoted sentence is an example of a question about one person and the group.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.oneToManyP.defaultMessage: Which of these people does this person know?
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.oneToManyP.description: Example question in the empty box where a researcher writes a One-to-Many Dyad Census prompt.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.ordinalBin.defaultMessage: Choose the gradient the bins run through, from the first value to the last.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.ordinalBin.description: Description of the group that picks the colour gradient the bins of an Ordinal Bin are shaded along.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.ordinalBin.defaultMessage: The bins are shaded along this gradient in the order the attribute lists its values.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.ordinalBin.description: Guidance under the control that picks the colour gradient the bins of an Ordinal Bin are shaded along.
Label of the control that picks the colour gradient the bins of an Ordinal Bin are shaded along.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.ordinalBin.defaultMessage: Choose the gradient the bins are shaded along.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.ordinalBin.description: Refusal shown when a researcher saves an Ordinal Bin prompt without a colour gradient for its bins.
Heading of the group that picks the colour gradient the bins of an Ordinal Bin are shaded along.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.ordinalBin.defaultMessage: The participant sorts everyone into ordered bins for one question at a time, in this order.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.ordinalBin.description: Guidance under the list of prompts in an Ordinal Bin stage, where the bins are a scale running from least to most and their order is what the answer means.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.ordinalBin.defaultMessage: The participant drags each person into one of a row of bins running from least to most, so write a question those bins are the scale of — “how often do you see this person?” rather than a yes or no question.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.ordinalBin.description: Guidance shown above the box where a researcher writes an Ordinal Bin prompt, saying what the participant does with it. The quoted sentence is an example of a question a scale can answer.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.ordinalBin.defaultMessage: This interface is designed for up to five bins. Beyond that the bins become hard to read and hard to drop into, which costs data quality.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.ordinalBin.description: Body of the warning shown when an Ordinal Bin prompt would draw more bins than its interview screen is designed for.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.ordinalBin.defaultMessage: How often do you have contact with this person?
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.ordinalBin.description: Example question in the empty box where a researcher writes an Ordinal Bin prompt.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.ordinalBin.defaultMessage: Choose the attribute whose ordered values the participant sorts people into.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.ordinalBin.description: Description of the group that picks the attribute whose ordered values are the bins the participant drags people into. An attribute is one thing an interview records about a network member.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.ordinalBin.defaultMessage: This type has no ordinal attributes yet. Create one to say what the scale is.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.ordinalBin.description: Shown in place of the attribute picker’s options when the node type this stage collects has no attribute whose answers run in an order.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.ordinalBin.defaultMessage: Each of this attribute's values becomes a bin, in the order the attribute lists them.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.ordinalBin.description: Guidance under the attribute picker in an Ordinal Bin prompt, saying that the attribute’s own order is the order of the bins.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.pairDescri.defaultMessage: Write the questions this stage asks about each pair, and drag them into the order the participant answers them.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.pairDescri.description: Description of the prompts section in a stage that shows the participant two network members side by side and asks about the two of them together. A stage is one step of an interview; a prompt is one question the participant is asked.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.pairFieldH.defaultMessage: The participant is shown one pair of people at a time and answers these questions about them, in this order.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.pairFieldH.description: Guidance under the list of prompts in a stage that shows the participant two network members side by side and asks about the two of them together.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.scaleTitle.description: Heading of the group that picks the attribute whose ordered values the participant answers on — the points running from least to most.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.sortRulesA.defaultMessage: Rules are applied in order. Use the asterisk to keep the order the people were added in.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.sortRulesA.description: Guidance under a list of sort rules whose fallback is the order the people were added to the network. The asterisk is the wildcard option offered in the rule’s own attribute picker.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.sortRulesD.defaultMessage: Rules are applied in order. Use the asterisk to keep the order the people were dropped in.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.sortRulesD.description: The same guidance for a list of sort rules inside a bin, where the fallback is the order the participant dragged people into that bin. The asterisk is the wildcard option offered in the rule’s own attribute picker.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.tieStrengt.defaultMessage: Give the participant a way to say these two people are not connected at all.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.tieStrengt.description: Description of the group holding the words the participant chooses to say the two people in front of them are not connected.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.tieStrengt.defaultMessage: Shown at the end of the scale. Choosing it records no connection between the pair.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.tieStrengt.description: Guidance under the box a researcher writes the decline answer into, saying where the participant sees it and what choosing it does.
Label of the box a researcher writes the words the participant chooses to say the two people are not connected.
Example wording in the empty box where a researcher writes the decline answer.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.tieStrengt.defaultMessage: Write how the participant says there is no connection.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.tieStrengt.description: Refusal shown when a researcher saves a Tie-Strength Census prompt without wording for the decline answer.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.tieStrengt.defaultMessage: Answering that there is no connection
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.tieStrengt.description: Heading of the group holding the words the participant chooses to say the two people in front of them are not connected.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.tieStrengt.defaultMessage: Choose the kind of connection an answer on the scale records between the pair.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.tieStrengt.description: Description of the group that says what answering on the scale records between the two people a Tie-Strength Census prompt asked about.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.tieStrengt.defaultMessage: A connection of this type is created between the two people whenever the participant answers on the scale.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.tieStrengt.description: Guidance under the control that picks what answering on the scale records between the two people a Tie-Strength Census prompt asked about.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.tieStrengt.defaultMessage: Choose the type of connection this prompt creates.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.tieStrengt.description: Refusal shown when a researcher saves a Tie-Strength Census prompt without saying what an answer on the scale records.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.tieStrengt.defaultMessage: The participant sees two people side by side and answers on a scale, so write the question about the pair in front of them — “how close are these two people?” rather than a name — and phrase it so that every point on the scale is a sensible answer.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.tieStrengt.description: Guidance shown above the box where a researcher writes a Tie-Strength Census prompt, saying what the participant is looking at while they answer it. The quoted sentence is an example of a question a scale can answer.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.tieStrengt.defaultMessage: How close are these two people?
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.tieStrengt.description: Example question in the empty box where a researcher writes a Tie-Strength Census prompt.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.tieStrengt.defaultMessage: Choose the attribute whose ordered values the participant answers on.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.tieStrengt.description: Description of the group that picks the attribute whose ordered values are the points of the scale. The attribute belongs to the connection this prompt creates, not to either person.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.tieStrengt.defaultMessage: This connection type has no ordinal attributes yet. Create one to say what the scale is.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.tieStrengt.description: Shown in place of the attribute picker’s options when the kind of connection this prompt creates has no attribute whose answers run in an order.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.tieStrengt.defaultMessage: The participant taps one of this attribute's values, and it is recorded on the connection.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.tieStrengt.description: Guidance under the attribute picker in a Tie-Strength Census prompt, saying where the participant’s answer is stored.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.tieStrengt.defaultMessage: This interface is designed for up to five points on the scale, with the decline answer beside them. Beyond that they become hard to read and hard to tap, which costs data quality.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.tieStrengt.description: Body of the warning shown when a Tie-Strength Census prompt would draw more points on its scale than its interview screen is designed for. The decline answer is the extra control the participant uses to say the two people are not connected.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.tieStrengt.defaultMessage: More answers than fit on one screen
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.tieStrengt.description: Heading of the warning shown when the attribute a Tie-Strength Census prompt uses offers more values than the interview screen can draw as points on its scale.

protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.tieStrengt.defaultMessage: Choose the attribute the participant answers on.
protocolBuilder.censusPrompts.tieStrengt.description: Refusal shown when a researcher saves a Tie-Strength Census prompt without saying which attribute holds the strength.

protocolBuilder.codebookEditing.createDe.description: What the change is called in the record a host keeps of protocol edits, and in any undo history it offers. name is the attribute name the researcher typed.

protocolBuilder.codebookEditing.createVa.defaultMessage: This attribute could not be created, so nothing was changed. Try again.
protocolBuilder.codebookEditing.createVa.description: Refusal shown on the attribute control of a stage editor when inventing a new attribute (a codebook variable) failed for a reason with no explanation of its own.

protocolBuilder.codebookEditing.missingT.defaultMessage: This type is no longer in the codebook, so an attribute cannot be added to it.
protocolBuilder.codebookEditing.missingT.description: Refusal shown when the node or edge type the stage works with has been deleted from the codebook — the protocol’s definition of what an interview records — while the researcher was editing.

protocolBuilder.codebookEditing.missingV.defaultMessage: This attribute is no longer in the codebook. Choose another one.
protocolBuilder.codebookEditing.missingV.description: Refusal shown on the attribute control of a stage editor when the attribute a row names has been deleted from the codebook while the researcher was editing.

protocolBuilder.codebookEditing.nameTake.defaultMessage: An attribute with this name already exists here. Choose another name.
protocolBuilder.codebookEditing.nameTake.description: Refusal shown under the name field when another attribute of the same type is already called that.

protocolBuilder.codebookEditing.newVaria.defaultMessage: Not a valid attribute name. Only letters, numbers and the symbols ._-: are supported
protocolBuilder.codebookEditing.newVaria.description: Refusal shown under the name field of a stage editor when the name typed for a new attribute holds characters the export formats cannot carry. The listed symbols are literal characters and must not be translated. Said in the same words as the row-cell rule that judges an attribute name as it is typed.

protocolBuilder.codebookEditing.noSubjec.defaultMessage: Choose what this stage works with before creating an attribute.
protocolBuilder.codebookEditing.noSubjec.description: Refusal shown when a researcher tries to invent an attribute before choosing which node or edge type the stage (one step of an interview) is about, so there is no codebook section to add it to.

protocolBuilder.codebookEditing.setCompo.description: What the change is called in the record a host keeps of protocol edits, and in any undo history it offers. name is the attribute’s researcher-facing name.

protocolBuilder.codebookEditing.setCompo.defaultMessage: This attribute’s input control could not be changed, so nothing was changed. Try again.
protocolBuilder.codebookEditing.setCompo.description: Refusal shown on the input-control dropdown of a stage editor when recording which control an attribute is collected with failed for a reason with no explanation of its own.

protocolBuilder.codebookEditing.unsuppor.defaultMessage: This attribute cannot be collected with that input control.
protocolBuilder.codebookEditing.unsuppor.description: Refusal shown on the input-control dropdown when the control chosen cannot collect the kind of answer this attribute holds.

protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.addEgoAtt.description: Button that adds the ego definition to a codebook that has none. The ego is the interview participant themselves.

protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.attribute.description: Accessible name of the list of one entity’s attributes (its codebook variables). name is the researcher’s own name for the node or edge type, or the word for the ego.
Heading over one entity’s attributes — the codebook variables recorded for it — on its card.

protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.codebookD.defaultMessage: Review entity types and the attributes each one owns.
protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.codebookD.description: Sentence under the codebook heading saying what the page is for. Entity types are the node and edge types a protocol defines; attributes are their codebook variables.

protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.codebookT.description: Heading of the page listing a protocol’s entity types and their attributes. The codebook is the protocol’s definition of what an interview records.

protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.colorHint.defaultMessage: {entity, select, node {Choose a color reference for this node type.} edge {Choose a color reference for this edge type.} other {Choose a color reference for this ego definition.}}
protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.colorHint.description: Guidance under the colour field. entity is node, edge or ego. A colour reference is a position in the protocol’s palette rather than a literal colour.

protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.colorLabe.description: Label of the field choosing which position in the protocol’s palette this entity type is drawn in.

protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.colorPlac.description: Placeholder shown in the colour field of the entity editor before a choice is made.

protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.createAtt.description: Visible label of the button that adds a new attribute (a codebook variable) to the entity this card is about.

protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.createAtt.defaultMessage: {entity, select, node {Create attribute for Node type: {name}} edge {Create attribute for Edge type: {name}} other {Create attribute for Ego attributes}}
protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.createAtt.description: Accessible name of the button that adds an attribute (a codebook variable) to one entity. entity is node, edge or ego; name is the researcher’s own name for that node or edge type. Names the card because the page shows one such button per card.

protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.createEdg.description: Button that adds a new edge type to the codebook. An edge is a relationship between two network members.

protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.createEnt.description: Accessible name of the group holding the buttons that add a node type, an edge type or the ego definition to the codebook.

protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.createNod.description: Button that adds a new node type to the codebook. A node is a member of the interview network.

protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.edgeTypes.description: Heading over the codebook’s edge types. An edge is a relationship between two network members.

protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.editAttri.description: Visible label of the button beside one attribute in an entity’s list. Its full accessible name names the attribute and the entity as well.

protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.editAttri.defaultMessage: {entity, select, node {Edit attribute {attributeName} for Node type: {name}} edge {Edit attribute {attributeName} for Edge type: {name}} other {Edit attribute {attributeName} for Ego attributes}}
protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.editAttri.description: Accessible name of the button that opens one attribute (a codebook variable) for editing. attributeName is the researcher’s own name for the attribute; entity is node, edge or ego; name is their own name for that node or edge type.

protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.editSubje.defaultMessage: {entity, select, node {Edit Node type: {name}} edge {Edit Edge type: {name}} other {Edit Ego attributes}}
protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.editSubje.description: Accessible name of the button that opens one codebook card for editing. entity is node, edge or ego; name is the researcher’s own name for that node or edge type. Names the card because the page shows one such button per card.

protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.editType.description: Button on a node or edge card that opens the type’s own properties — its name, colour and appearance.

protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.egoHeadin.description: The word for the interview participant themselves, used both as the heading over their section of the codebook and as the name of their card.

protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.iconHint.defaultMessage: Enter the Lucide or Network Canvas icon name shown by interfaces that create this type.
protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.iconHint.description: Guidance under the icon field. "Lucide" is an icon library and "Network Canvas" the product; both are names and stay as they are. An interface is one kind of interview step.

protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.iconLabel.description: Label of the field naming the icon shown on the buttons an interview offers for creating this node type. An interface is one kind of interview step.

protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.issuesLis.description: Accessible name of the list of parts of the stored codebook this page could not read.

protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.issuesTit.defaultMessage: Some codebook data could not be displayed
protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.issuesTit.description: Heading of the warning listing parts of the stored codebook this page could not read.

protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.manageEgo.description: Button on the ego card that opens its attribute list. The ego — the interview participant themselves — has attributes but no type properties, so the button offers those rather than editing a type.

protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.nameHint.defaultMessage: {entity, select, node {This name identifies the node type in the codebook and exported data.} edge {This name identifies the edge type in the codebook and exported data.} other {This name identifies the ego definition in the codebook and exported data.}}
protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.nameHint.description: Guidance under the name field, saying where the name is read back. entity is node, edge or ego. The codebook is the protocol’s definition of what an interview records; exported data is the file a researcher analyses afterwards.

protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.nameLabel.defaultMessage: {entity, select, node {Node type name} other {Edge type name}}
protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.nameLabel.description: Label of the field holding the researcher’s own name for this entity type. entity is node or edge; the ego has no type name.

protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.noAttribu.description: Shown on an entity’s card in place of its attribute list when the entity records none yet.

protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.noEdgeTyp.defaultMessage: No valid edge types are available.
protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.noEdgeTyp.description: Shown in place of the edge type list when the codebook defines none this page can read.

protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.noEgoDefi.defaultMessage: No valid ego definition is available.
protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.noEgoDefi.description: Shown in place of the ego card when the codebook holds no ego definition this page can read. The ego is the interview participant themselves.

protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.noNodeTyp.defaultMessage: No valid node types are available.
protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.noNodeTyp.description: Shown in place of the node type list when the codebook defines none this page can read.

protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.nodeTypes.description: Heading over the codebook’s node types. A node is a member of the interview network.

protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.shapeHint.defaultMessage: Choose the shape used when no dynamic shape mapping applies.
protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.shapeHint.description: Guidance under the shape field. A dynamic shape mapping is a protocol rule that draws a node differently depending on one of its attributes.

protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.shapeLabe.description: Label of the field choosing the shape a node type is drawn as when nothing overrides it.

protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.shapePlac.description: Placeholder shown in the shape field of the node type editor before a choice is made.

protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.subjectDe.defaultMessage: {entity, select, node {Node type: {name}} edge {Edge type: {name}} other {Ego attributes}}
protocolBuilder.codebookEntity.subjectDe.description: Names one card of the codebook overview, and is the card’s accessible name. entity is node, edge or ego; name is the researcher’s own name for that node or edge type. The ego is the interview participant themselves, and has attributes but no type name.

protocolBuilder.codebookVariable.boolean.description: Label of the field holding the words on one of the two answers a yes/no attribute offers. records says which of the two stored values this answer records; “true” and “false” are the literal values the protocol stores and an export records, so they stay as they are.

Placeholder in the field holding the words on one of the two answers a yes/no attribute offers, shown while the researcher has written none. It has to read exactly as the interview’s own yes/no control does for an attribute that names no answers — frescoUi.booleanField.yes and frescoUi.booleanField.no — because that is literally what the participant will see. records says which of the two stored values this answer records.

protocolBuilder.codebookVariable.boolean.defaultMessage: {records, select, true {Style “true” as negative} other {Style “false” as negative}}
protocolBuilder.codebookVariable.boolean.description: Label of the switch that draws one of the two answers of a yes/no attribute in red when a participant selects it. records says which of the two stored values this answer records; “true” and “false” are the literal values the protocol stores and stay as they are.

protocolBuilder.codebookVariable.nameHin.defaultMessage: This name is used when referring to the attribute and in exported data.
protocolBuilder.codebookVariable.nameHin.description: Guidance under the attribute name field. Exported data is the file a researcher analyses after the interviews.

protocolBuilder.codebookVariable.nameLab.description: Label of the field holding the researcher’s own name for this attribute (a codebook variable).

protocolBuilder.codebookVariable.optionL.description: Label of the field holding what a participant reads for one allowed answer. index is that answer’s position in the list, counting from one, and is passed as text because the researcher reads it as this row’s name.

protocolBuilder.codebookVariable.optionV.description: Label of the field holding what the export records for one allowed answer. index is that answer’s position in the list, counting from one, and is passed as text because the researcher reads it as this row’s name.

protocolBuilder.codebookVariable.removeO.description: Accessible name of the button that deletes one allowed answer. index is that answer’s position in the list, counting from one, and is passed as text because the researcher reads it as this row’s name.

protocolBuilder.codebookVariable.repeate.defaultMessage: Give this answer different words: two buttons saying the same thing cannot be told apart.
protocolBuilder.codebookVariable.repeate.description: Refusal shown under the second of the two answers of a yes/no attribute when both have been given the same words, which leaves the participant two buttons they cannot tell apart.

protocolBuilder.codebookVariable.typeLab.description: Label of the field choosing what kind of answer this attribute records.

protocolBuilder.codebookVariable.typePla.description: Placeholder shown in the attribute type field before a choice is made.

protocolBuilder.codebookVariable.unnamed.defaultMessage: Write what this answer says, or clear both to offer Yes and No.
protocolBuilder.codebookVariable.unnamed.description: Refusal shown under one of the two answers of a yes/no attribute when it has been left blank while the other is written. Clearing both is a real answer: an attribute that names neither is offered to the participant as Yes and No.

protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.compound.defaultMessage: Another change to the codebook is still being saved. Wait for it to finish, then save this one.
protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.compound.description: Refusal shown in a codebook editor when a previous change to the codebook — the protocol’s definition of what an interview records — has not finished saving.

protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.heldBy.defaultMessage: {holder} is currently editing a section needed for this change.
protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.heldBy.description: Refusal shown in a codebook editor when a named collaborator is editing part of the protocol the change needs. holder is that person’s display name, which the host supplies.

protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.heldBySo.defaultMessage: A section needed for this change is currently being edited.
protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.heldBySo.description: Refusal shown in a codebook editor when part of the protocol the change needs is being edited by somebody the host would not name.

protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.hostErro.defaultMessage: The protocol would not be valid with this change, so nothing was saved. Adjust this type and try again, or close this and come back once the rest of the stage is filled in.
protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.hostErro.description: Refusal shown in a codebook editor when the change would leave the whole protocol invalid — usually because the stage being configured is not finished yet. A stage is one step of an interview.

protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.invalidR.defaultMessage: This change could not be sent, and nothing was saved. Close this editor and try again.
protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.invalidR.description: Refusal shown in a codebook editor when the change could not be sent for saving at all.

protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.invalidR.defaultMessage: The protocol came back in a state this editor cannot read, so nothing here has been kept. Reload the protocol before making this change.
protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.invalidR.description: Refusal shown in a codebook editor when what came back after saving was not something the editor could read.

protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.leaseLos.defaultMessage: You are no longer the editor of this stage, so nothing was saved. Take over editing and try again.
protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.leaseLos.description: Refusal shown in a codebook editor when the researcher no longer holds the right to edit this stage. Taking over editing is an action offered elsewhere in the host application.

protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.pendingC.defaultMessage: A file you added is still waiting to be saved with this stage. Save the stage first, then make this change.
protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.pendingC.description: Refusal shown in a codebook editor when the stage still holds an imported file that has not been saved, which has to land before the codebook can change.

protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.staleBas.defaultMessage: Someone else changed this while you were editing it, so nothing was saved. Close and reopen this editor to load their version, then make your change again.
protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.staleBas.description: Refusal shown in a codebook editor when a collaborator changed the same thing while this editor was open.

protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.staleEpo.defaultMessage: Editing access changed while this was being saved, so nothing was saved. Try again.
protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.staleEpo.description: Refusal shown in a codebook editor when who holds the right to edit changed midway through saving.

protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.staleRes.defaultMessage: A newer version of the protocol is already open, so this change was not applied. Try again.
protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.staleRes.description: Refusal shown in a codebook editor when a newer version of the protocol had already been loaded by the time the change came back.

protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.unavaila.defaultMessage: This editor cannot change the codebook right now. Reload the protocol and try again.
protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.unavaila.description: Refusal shown in a codebook editor when the host cannot accept codebook changes at all just now.

protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.unexplai.defaultMessage: This change could not be saved, and nothing was altered. Wait a moment and try again.
protocolBuilder.compoundFailure.unexplai.description: Refusal shown in a codebook editor when saving threw with no explanation a researcher could act on. The last resort.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.audioHint.defaultMessage: The audio the participant can play when they reach this block.
protocolBuilder.contentBlock.audioHint.description: Guidance under the file picker of a block that plays an audio recording.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.audioRequir.defaultMessage: Choose the audio file this block plays.
protocolBuilder.contentBlock.audioRequir.description: Refusal shown under the file picker of an audio block when nothing has been chosen.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.contentLabe.description: Label of the control holding what one piece of a page actually shows, whichever kind it is.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.imageHint.defaultMessage: The image the participant sees when they reach this block.
protocolBuilder.contentBlock.imageHint.description: Guidance under the file picker of a block that shows a picture.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.imageRequir.defaultMessage: Choose the image this block shows.
protocolBuilder.contentBlock.imageRequir.description: Refusal shown under the file picker of a picture block when nothing has been chosen.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.kindAudio.description: Choice offered for what one piece of a page holds: an audio recording.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.kindChanged.defaultMessage: Content type changed to {kind}. Nothing has been entered for {kind} yet.
protocolBuilder.contentBlock.kindChanged.description: Announcement made when a researcher changes what kind of thing one piece of a page holds and neither the old nor the new kind has anything in it. kind is the new choice, already in the reader’s language.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.kindChanged.defaultMessage: Content type changed to {kind}. The content you entered for the previous type is kept, and returns if you change back to it.
protocolBuilder.contentBlock.kindChanged.description: Announcement made when a researcher changes what kind of thing one piece of a page holds, away from a kind they had filled in, which is kept rather than thrown away. kind is the new choice, already in the reader’s language.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.kindChanged.defaultMessage: Content type changed to {kind}. The content you entered for {kind} earlier has been restored.
protocolBuilder.contentBlock.kindChanged.description: Announcement made when a researcher changes what kind of thing one piece of a page holds, back to a kind they had already filled in, so their earlier answer comes back. kind is that choice, already in the reader’s language.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.kindChosen.defaultMessage: Content type set to {kind}. A content field for it has been added below.
protocolBuilder.contentBlock.kindChosen.description: Announcement made when a researcher first says what kind of thing one piece of a page holds, which mounts a control for it. kind is that choice — Image, Video, Audio, Text — already in the reader’s language.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.kindHint.defaultMessage: Choose what this block shows the participant.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.kindImage.description: Choice offered for what one piece of a page holds: a picture.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.kindLabel.description: Label of the control choosing what kind of thing one piece of a page holds — a picture, a video, an audio recording, prose.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.kindRequire.defaultMessage: Choose what kind of content this block holds.
protocolBuilder.contentBlock.kindRequire.description: Refusal shown under the content-type control when the researcher has chosen nothing.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.kindText.description: Choice offered for what one piece of a page holds: prose the participant reads.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.kindVideo.description: Choice offered for what one piece of a page holds: a video.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.missingReso.defaultMessage: This block’s resource is no longer in this protocol. Choose a content type above to replace it.
protocolBuilder.contentBlock.missingReso.description: Warning body shown when a piece of a page points at a file that has been deleted from the protocol, so it needs replacing.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.previewEmpt.defaultMessage: This block has no content yet.
protocolBuilder.contentBlock.previewEmpt.description: Shown in the collapsed row of a page’s list of blocks when the researcher has not yet said what that piece of the page holds.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.previewUnus.defaultMessage: This block’s resource is not in this protocol, or is not something a page can show.
protocolBuilder.contentBlock.previewUnus.description: Shown in the collapsed row of a page’s list of blocks when that piece points at a file the protocol no longer holds, or at one a page cannot present — a roster of people, a map layer, a key.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.sectionDesc.defaultMessage: Choose what kind of content this block holds, and provide the content itself.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.sectionTitl.description: Heading of the dialog where a researcher says what one piece of a page holds and provides it.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.sizeFull.description: Choice offered for how tall a picture or video on a page is drawn: however tall it naturally is, unconstrained.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.sizeHint.defaultMessage: Optionally constrain the height of this block. Full size lets it show at its natural height.
protocolBuilder.contentBlock.sizeHint.description: Guidance under the display-size control. "Full size" is the wording of the unconstrained choice it offers.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.sizeLabel.description: Label of the control constraining how tall a picture or video is drawn on a page.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.sizeLarge.description: Choice offered for how tall a picture or video on a page is drawn.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.sizeMedium.description: Choice offered for how tall a picture or video on a page is drawn.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.sizeSmall.description: Choice offered for how tall a picture or video on a page is drawn.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.textHint.defaultMessage: What the participant reads when they reach this block. Supports markdown formatting.
protocolBuilder.contentBlock.textHint.description: Guidance under the control holding the prose of a text block. Markdown is the name of the formatting syntax and is not translated.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.textPlaceho.defaultMessage: Enter the text for this block...
protocolBuilder.contentBlock.textPlaceho.description: Placeholder shown in the empty prose control of a text block. The trailing dots are an ellipsis written as three full stops.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.textRequire.defaultMessage: Write the text this block shows.
protocolBuilder.contentBlock.textRequire.description: Refusal shown under the prose control of a text block when it has been left empty.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.unpresentab.defaultMessage: This block’s resource is not an image, audio or video file, so this block cannot show it. Choose a content type above to replace it.
protocolBuilder.contentBlock.unpresentab.description: Warning body shown when a piece of a page points at a file that IS in the protocol but is not something a page can present — a roster of people, a map layer, a key. Distinct from a deleted file, because there is nothing missing to go looking for.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.unusableTit.description: Warning heading shown when a piece of a page points at a file the page cannot present.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.videoHint.defaultMessage: The video the participant can play when they reach this block.
protocolBuilder.contentBlock.videoHint.description: Guidance under the file picker of a block that plays a video.

protocolBuilder.contentBlock.videoRequir.defaultMessage: Choose the video this block plays.
protocolBuilder.contentBlock.videoRequir.description: Refusal shown under the file picker of a video block when nothing has been chosen.

protocolBuilder.dialogForm.discardConfir.description: Button that closes an editing dialog and throws away the unsaved work in it.

protocolBuilder.dialogForm.discardDescri.defaultMessage: This editor holds changes that have not been saved. Closing it now discards them.
protocolBuilder.dialogForm.discardDescri.description: Body of the confirmation raised when a researcher tries to close an editing dialog that holds unsaved work.

protocolBuilder.dialogForm.discardTitle.description: Title of the confirmation raised when a researcher tries to close an editing dialog that holds unsaved work.

protocolBuilder.dialogForm.keepEditing.description: Button that dismisses the discard confirmation and leaves the editing dialog open with its unsaved work intact.

protocolBuilder.dialogForm.resizeHandle.description: Accessible name of the divider a researcher drags to give more room either to the fields of an editing dialog or to the live preview beside them.

protocolBuilder.formFields.addLabel.description: Button that opens the dialog for adding one more question to a form. Whole rather than a generic "Add", because a stage editor shows several lists at once.

protocolBuilder.formFields.addTitle.description: Title of the dialog a researcher fills in to add one more question to a form.

protocolBuilder.formFields.atLeastOne.defaultMessage: Add at least one field. A form with no fields collects nothing.
protocolBuilder.formFields.atLeastOne.description: Refusal shown above a form’s list of fields when a researcher saves a form that asks nothing. A field is one question bound to one attribute of a network member.

protocolBuilder.formFields.attributeEmpt.defaultMessage: Every attribute of this type is already collected or written elsewhere. Create a new one instead.
protocolBuilder.formFields.attributeEmpt.description: Shown in place of the attribute list when every attribute of this node or edge type is either already collected by another field of the same form, or written somewhere the protocol will not let a form field also write.

protocolBuilder.formFields.attributeHint.defaultMessage: The codebook attribute this field’s answer is stored in.
protocolBuilder.formFields.attributeHint.description: Guidance under the attribute control. The codebook is the protocol’s definition of what an interview records.

protocolBuilder.formFields.attributeLabe.description: Label of the control choosing which attribute this question’s answer is recorded under. The same word as the section heading above it, and translated once for each.

protocolBuilder.formFields.attributeRequ.defaultMessage: Choose the attribute this field collects.
protocolBuilder.formFields.attributeRequ.description: Refusal shown under the attribute control when nothing has been chosen.

protocolBuilder.formFields.attributeSect.defaultMessage: Choose the attribute this field collects, or create one for it.

protocolBuilder.formFields.attributeSect.description: Heading of the half of the field dialog that says which attribute this question’s answer is recorded under.

protocolBuilder.formFields.attributeTake.defaultMessage: Another field in this form already collects this attribute. Choose a different one, or edit that field instead.
protocolBuilder.formFields.attributeTake.description: Refusal shown under the attribute control when a sibling field of the same form already records its answer under the attribute just chosen.

protocolBuilder.formFields.componentHint.defaultMessage: What the participant uses to answer. Changing it changes how this attribute is collected everywhere.
protocolBuilder.formFields.componentHint.description: Guidance under the input-control field, warning that the control belongs to the attribute rather than to this one question.

protocolBuilder.formFields.componentLabe.description: Label of the control choosing what the participant uses to answer — a text box, a slider, a set of buttons.

protocolBuilder.formFields.componentRequ.defaultMessage: Choose how the participant answers this field.
protocolBuilder.formFields.componentRequ.description: Refusal shown under the input-control field when nothing has been chosen.

protocolBuilder.formFields.createNewOpti.description: The last choice in the attribute list, which stands for an attribute that does not exist yet and asks the researcher to name one. The trailing character is an ellipsis.

protocolBuilder.formFields.createWithVal.defaultMessage: Create this attribute and the values it offers before adding the field that collects it.
protocolBuilder.formFields.createWithVal.description: Refusal shown under the kind-of-answer control when a researcher tries to invent an attribute whose answers come from a list, which cannot be made from a name and a kind alone.

protocolBuilder.formFields.description.defaultMessage: Choose the attributes this form collects, and write the question the participant answers for each.

protocolBuilder.formFields.duplicateFiel.defaultMessage: Two fields collect the same attribute. Each attribute may be collected once per form.
protocolBuilder.formFields.duplicateFiel.description: Refusal shown above a form’s list of fields when two of them record their answers under the same attribute, which would leave only one of the answers.

protocolBuilder.formFields.editTitle.description: Title of the dialog a researcher fills in to change a question a form already asks.

protocolBuilder.formFields.emptyState.defaultMessage: No fields yet. Create one to say what this form collects.
protocolBuilder.formFields.emptyState.description: Shown in place of the list of form fields while a form asks nothing yet.

protocolBuilder.formFields.fieldHint.defaultMessage: The participant answers these one after another, in this order. Add at least one.
protocolBuilder.formFields.fieldHint.description: Guidance under the list of form fields.

protocolBuilder.formFields.fieldLabel.description: Label of the ordered list of questions a form asks.

protocolBuilder.formFields.formTitleHint.defaultMessage: Shown above the form. Use a short phrase describing what it collects, such as "Add a person".
protocolBuilder.formFields.formTitleHint.description: Guidance under the form-title field. The quoted phrase is an example a researcher might write, and should be translated as such.

protocolBuilder.formFields.formTitleLabe.description: Label of the field holding the heading shown above the form a participant fills in.

protocolBuilder.formFields.formTitlePlac.description: Example form title shown in the empty field. An example a researcher might write, not a value that is stored.

protocolBuilder.formFields.formTitleRequ.description: Refusal shown under the form-title field when it has been left empty.

protocolBuilder.formFields.hintHint.defaultMessage: Optional guidance shown below the question, for a field participants may find ambiguous.

protocolBuilder.formFields.hintLabel.description: Label of the optional field holding extra guidance shown to the participant under the question.

protocolBuilder.formFields.hintPlacehold.description: Example hint shown in the empty hint-text field. An example a researcher might write, not a value that is stored.

protocolBuilder.formFields.incompleteFie.defaultMessage: Every field needs both an attribute and a question. Open the incomplete field and finish it.
protocolBuilder.formFields.incompleteFie.description: Refusal shown above a form’s list of fields when one of them names no attribute, or asks no question.

protocolBuilder.formFields.itemNoun.description: What one row of a form’s list of questions is called inside things said ABOUT it — "Edit field", "Remove this field?" — so it is lower case and singular.

protocolBuilder.formFields.newNameHint.defaultMessage: How this attribute is named in the codebook and in exported data.
protocolBuilder.formFields.newNameHint.description: Guidance under the new-attribute name field. The codebook is the protocol’s definition of what an interview records; exported data is the file a researcher analyzes afterwards.

protocolBuilder.formFields.newNameLabel.description: Label of the field naming an attribute the researcher is inventing.

protocolBuilder.formFields.newNamePlaceh.description: Example attribute name shown in the empty field. An example a researcher might write, not a value that is stored.

protocolBuilder.formFields.newNameRequir.defaultMessage: Name the attribute this field collects.
protocolBuilder.formFields.newNameRequir.description: Refusal shown under the new-attribute name field when it has been left empty.

protocolBuilder.formFields.newTypeHint.defaultMessage: What this attribute holds. It cannot be changed once answers have been collected.

protocolBuilder.formFields.newTypeLabel.description: Label of the control choosing what sort of value a new attribute holds — text, a number, a date, a choice from a list.

protocolBuilder.formFields.newTypeRequir.defaultMessage: Choose what kind of answer this attribute holds.
protocolBuilder.formFields.newTypeRequir.description: Refusal shown under the kind-of-answer control when nothing has been chosen.

protocolBuilder.formFields.previewCollec.description: Shown in the collapsed row of a form’s list of questions, saying which attribute it records into and what kind of value that holds. name is the attribute’s researcher-facing name; type is a schema token such as text, number or ordinal, which is not translated.

protocolBuilder.formFields.previewMissin.defaultMessage: This attribute is no longer in the codebook.
protocolBuilder.formFields.previewMissin.description: Shown in the collapsed row of a form’s list of questions when the attribute it records into has been deleted from the codebook.

protocolBuilder.formFields.promptHint.defaultMessage: Shown to the participant above the control. Supports markdown formatting.
protocolBuilder.formFields.promptHint.description: Guidance under the question-text field. Markdown is the name of the formatting syntax and is not translated.

protocolBuilder.formFields.promptLabel.description: Label of the field holding what the participant is asked for this one answer.

protocolBuilder.formFields.promptPlaceho.description: Example question shown in the empty question-text field. An example a researcher might write, not a value that is stored.

protocolBuilder.formFields.promptRequire.defaultMessage: Write the question this field asks.
protocolBuilder.formFields.promptRequire.description: Refusal shown under the question-text field when it has been left empty.

protocolBuilder.formFields.questionSecti.defaultMessage: Write what the participant is asked, and how much help they are given.
